sections.title: List
rows: a branch: open its PR review · a section header: fold or unfold it
give the keyboard back to the work area

sections.title: Filters (shift: previous value)
rows: show / hide the filters (the filter button counts the ones changed)
status: active, open, draft, merged, closed, all
review: requested from me, changes requested, …

sections.title: Move
rows: next / previous item; in Files, the diff jumps to that file
open the item (a commit: its diff in Files; a check or comment: on GitHub); in Files, go into the diff
back from the diff to the file list
previous / next linked repo (or click its chip)
the PR below / above this one in its GitHub stack, in its own tab (or click its chip in the Stack row)
leave search, then clear it, then leave a commit's diff, then close the tab

sections.title: Act on the shown PR
rows: comment (a, x and c open a Markdown box: enter is a new line, cmd-enter sends, ctrl-shift-p switches Write / Preview, esc cancels)
merge with a merge commit (press twice); a stacked PR merges with the open PRs below it
restack (press twice): rebase each open PR of the stack onto the one below, the bottom onto the base, and force-push what moved; a ⚠ on a stack chip marks a PR that needs it
ready for review / back to draft
pick reviewers: space/x tick, / search, enter save, esc cancel (who reviewed already comes after the requested; tick them to re-request)
Blueprint of this branch beside the review
walkthrough of this PR, or of every linked PR as one change (Claude explains the diff step by step, in reading order)
